The Houses

A storybook universe of family houses, each one narrating the family that shares it.

Playful on the surface. Nostalgic underneath. More time at the place you love.

SummaryWho we areThe universeCharactersSeriesNext 10 episodesHow we show upProduction & costMeasurement90-day roadmapDecisions

Executive summary

We are not running ads. We are building a following, and eventually a small piece of IP, by putting out fun, warm family content about the places families share. SplitHaus is the studio behind it, not the star.

What

Three stop-motion-style houses (a lake cabin, a ski chalet, a beach cottage), each narrating its family. A recurring series for every character, plus cheap static posts in between.

Why this works

Our audience is older, nostalgic and family-centered. People follow accounts that make them feel seen and give them something to send the family group chat, which is also the top thing Instagram rewards.

Why characters, not AI humans

Cheaper to make, no uncanny-valley backlash, Instagram now limits reach for undisclosed AI-generated people, and characters are IP we own and can extend.

Where

Instagram home base, cross-posted to Facebook (where our buyers are). TikTok for the cousin generation, YouTube Shorts as free reach, Pinterest for rules and checklists, X kept light.

Cadence

~5 feed posts a week: 2 episodes, 2 static posts, 1 community post, plus daily Stories. Product in about 1 post in 8.

Cost

~$50–100/month in generation and tools. The real cost is ~2 hrs/week review plus ~20 min/day answering the community.

Who we are online

The home of families who share a house. We tell their stories, their fights, their rules and their traditions, with affection for every character, including the difficult ones.

Ad-shaped (what we're moving away from)

  • Story exists to deliver the product
  • Ends on a logo and a tagline
  • Measured by sign-ups
  • Talks about us

Following-shaped (what we're building)

  • Story exists because it's funny or true
  • Ends on a question or a 'send this to…' beat
  • Measured by sends, follows, saves, submissions
  • Talks about them: their house, their family

Brand voice

We areWe are not
Warm, wry, nostalgic, a little mischievousSalesy, snarky at the audience, cynical
Specific (the creaky swing, the outdoor shower, the mitten)Generic 'family time' stock sentiment
On everyone's side, even Dave'sMocking any family member or generation
Clearly animated, clearly fictionalPretending to be real people or real customers
Non-negotiable rules.
  • Stylized puppets only. No photoreal AI people, no AI spokesperson.
  • Label fiction ('a fictional family') and turn on platform AI labels.
  • No fake testimonials, fake customer counts or invented follower submissions.
  • No legal, estate, tax or ownership advice. We talk about sharing time, not title.
  • No real property, address or family from our prospect research ever appears in content.

Bio (draft)

Stories, rules & traditions from families who share a house. 🏡 Narrated by the houses. Lake · Mountain · Beach. Send us your house rules ↓
Link: free 'Family House Rules' template + newsletter. Highlights: Meet the Families · House Rules · Send Us Yours.

The universe: one house per region

Same felt-diorama world, three regions, three seasons. Each house has its own narrator voice, family and signature fight. We launch the lake, add the mountain for ski season, and the beach for summer-planning season. Gulf, West Coast and farmhouse stay on the shelf until one of these is clearly working.

Northwoods lake country (Minnesota / Wisconsin / Michigan)

The Cabin at Loon Point · built 1956

Signature fight: Who gets the Fourth of July.

Narrator voice: Warm, dry, older man. Unhurried, faintly amused. Has seen 70 summers of family politics and loves every one of them.

Family: The Hallorans. Grandma June and her late husband Walt bought the cabin in 1956. Three branches now share it.

Season: Summer (peak), fall closing-up, spring opening

Look: Cedar shingles, forest-green trim, stone chimney, screened porch with a creaky swing, red canoe, dock with two white Adirondack chairs, flag bunting. Palette: cedar, lake blue, cream, pine.

Vermont ski country (translates to Rockies / Tahoe / Utah)

Windhill · built 1971

Signature fight: Who gets Christmas week (and who gets the powder days).

Narrator voice: Crisp, cheerful, a little proud. An A-frame who still thinks it's the coolest house on the mountain. Speaks in weather.

Family: The Lindqvists. Big Tom built Windhill with his brothers in 1971. His daughter-in-law Priya, who married in, now keeps the whole thing running.

Season: Winter (peak): first snow → Christmas week → Presidents' Day; summer is quiet

Look: Steep A-frame roof heavy with snow, giant glowing triangular window, red door, firewood under the eave, old wooden skis by the door. Palette: snow white, amber window light, cedar, cranberry red.

East Coast beach (Cape Cod; translates to Outer Banks / Jersey Shore / Maine)

Fair Winds · built 1948

Signature fight: Who gets August (and who leaves sand in the outdoor shower).

Narrator voice: Salty, gentle, a little romantic. An old cottage who measures time in tides and sand on the floor.

Family: The Costas. Pop bought Fair Winds in 1948 with his late wife Dot after the war. Two daughters' families and a brother-in-law share it.

Season: Summer (peak), with a Feb–Apr planning season when families fight over August

Look: Silver-grey shingles, white trim, faded blue shutters, blue hydrangeas, picket fence, outdoor shower, dune path to the water. Palette: weathered grey, hydrangea blue, sand, sea-glass green.

Characters

Sketches are first-pass concept art generated in our felt-puppet style (the Lake family images are the production reference sheets from Episode 1). Personalities, wants and fears drive every episode; the one-liners set each voice.

The Cabin at Loon Point

Narrator · Built 1956

The House

Personality
Patient, wry, deeply sentimental underneath. Remembers everything: every sunburn, every slammed screen door, every height mark on the kitchen door frame.
Wants
Everyone here. Every summer. For another seventy.
Fears
The summer nobody comes. The 'For Sale' sign.
Quirk
Creaks at the exact wrong moment. Keeps score of the family's fights like baseball stats.

Ruth Halloran

Personality
Capable, over-extended, quietly funny. The one who keeps the spreadsheet, answers the group text, buys the propane and never gets thanked. Fair to a fault.

Series: ten per house

Each series has a fixed format and, once live, a fixed weekday, so followers come back for it. We won't run all 30 at once: launch with 3–4 per active house, keep the ones with the best sends and follows, retire the rest.

Across the universe

House Rules (all houses)

Followers submit their family's real rules and fights; the best become carousels and episode plots. The flywheel.

Which Character Are You?

Quizzes, polls and 'tag your Dave' posts across all three houses. Built for sends.

Letters Between Houses

The three houses write each other postcards across the seasons (the cabin to the chalet in January, the cottage to the cabin in August). Ties the universe together; great static carousels.

Lake, Mountain or Beach?

Recurring Stories polls and debate posts. Segments the audience by house.

The next 10 episodes

October through early February, timed to real seasons: closing the cabin, first snow, Christmas week, New Year, then summer-planning season for the beach. Roughly 60% comedy, 40% heartstrings. Every episode ends on a question to the audience, not a logo. Each ships with a companion static post.

01

Who Gets the Fourth? (re-cut)

The Cabin at Loon PointWho Gets the Fourth?ComedyLaunch week (early Oct)30–35s

Seventy summers, one Fourth of July, and a family that has never agreed on who gets it.

  1. Cold open on Dave: 'Dave has had the Fourth since 1994.'
  2. The cabin at golden hour; the House introduces itself.
  3. Ruth buried in the paper calendar.
  4. The cousins' protest sign: 'FAIR TURNS NOW'.
  5. June with the 1978 photo: 'She just wants everyone here. Once.'
  6. Ruth writes the rules down where everyone can see them.
  7. Fireworks; 'Nobody argued. Well… Dave argued.'
Opening line: “Dave has had the Fourth since 1994. Nobody remembers agreeing to that.”  ·  Ending question: “Who gets the Fourth at your house?”
Companion static: Character intro cards (5) + 'Who's the Dave in your family?' quote card.
Production: Existing clips; re-narrate line 6; drop the logo end card.  ·  Est. generation cost: ~$0–3
02

Closing Day

The Cabin at Loon PointJune RemembersHeartstringsMid-Oct (real closing season)25–30s

The last morning of the season. June closes the cabin for what she suspects might be the last time she does it herself.

  1. Frost on the dock; Adirondack chairs stacked.
  2. June runs her hand over the kitchen door frame height marks.
  3. She finds Walt's handwriting: 'Dave, 1966'.
  4. Dave quietly carries her bag and says nothing, for once.
  5. The House: 'She says see you in May. She always says see you in May.'
Opening line: “Every October, June is the last one out.”  ·  Ending question: “What's the last thing your family does before closing up?”
Companion static: Carousel: 'The closing-day checklist every cabin family knows.'
Production: 2 animated shots (hand on door frame, Dave with bag); rest stills + pan.  ·  Est. generation cost: ~$2–4
03

The Hot Dog Flag

The Cabin at Loon PointDave's TraditionsComedyLate Oct20–30s

The true, deeply stupid origin of Dave's sacred Fourth of July hot-dog flag.

  1. Dave, solemn: 'The flag goes in the hot dog. It always has.'
  2. Flashback, 1994: the only flag they could find was a toothpick flag from a sandwich.
  3. Maya: 'So it's not a tradition, it's a sandwich.'
  4. Dave, softer: it was Walt's last Fourth.
  5. Beat. Everyone puts a flag in their hot dog.
Opening line: “Every family has one tradition nobody is allowed to question.”  ·  Ending question: “What's the tradition in your family nobody's allowed to question?”
Companion static: Quote card: 'We've always done it this way.' (They have not.)
Production: Flashback as sepia-tinted stills; 1–2 animated shots.  ·  Est. generation cost: ~$1–3

Who Gets August?

Fair WindsWho Gets August?ComedyEarly Feb (summer planning season)30–35s

Carol's laminated rules vs. Meg's January booking vs. Annie's 'I'll just show up' vs. Richie's 'I'm basically gone'.

  1. Carol blows the whistle: August planning meeting.
  2. Meg slides over a calendar booked in January.
  3. Annie: 'I didn't take your week, I joined it.'
  4. Richie, from the lawn chair: 'I'll be out by Tuesday.' (Title card: he was not.)
  5. Carol laminates the final schedule. Gerald steals it.
Opening line: “Every February, this family goes to war over August.”  ·  Ending question: “Who gets August at your beach house?”
Companion static: Carol's Laminated Rules carousel: 'The 5 beach-house rules every family needs.'
Production: 3 animated shots max (Gerald shot is the hero).  ·  Est. generation cost: ~$2–4
Heartstring story bank (for later episodes): the first grandchild's first swim · the summer after Grandpa · the last summer before a sibling wants to sell · the guestbook entries from 1978 · everyone at the lake for June's 90th · Pop's last sail · Big Tom's final first chair · the hurricane that almost took Fair Winds · the dog that waited on the dock.

Start at ~5 feed posts/week total. Consistency beats volume.

Talking to people

  • Replies come from the House, in first person: warm, short, curious ('Tell me about your dock.').
  • Ask for a rule or a memory in every caption.
  • Feature submissions weekly, with permission, redrawn in house style.
  • Never argue; never sell in the comments.

Growing without ads

  • Design every post to be sent to a family chat (Instagram weighs sends per reach heavily).
  • Trial Reels: test episodes on non-followers first; post winners to the grid.
  • Collab posts with lake-life, ski-town, beach-house and cottage-interior accounts. Regional houses make this natural.
  • Groups and Reddit: participate as people, never link-drop. Listen for stories.
  • Owned list from day 1: free 'Family House Rules' template and a short newsletter ('Letters from the Houses').

Where SplitHaus shows up

About 1 post in 8, only where it's genuinely the answer: Ruth's Rules, Priya's Keys and Carol's Laminated Rules carousels, the bio link, and the newsletter. Never in the heartstring episodes.

Protecting the IP

  • Maintain a character bible (names, backstories, voices, reference sheets, house histories).
  • Humans write the scripts and make the character decisions. Purely AI-generated imagery has limited US copyright protection; scripts, names and developed characters are what we can protect.
  • Trademark the series name(s) once one takes off.
  • One consistent voice per house, locked early.

Production & cost

Lessons from the Episode 1 pilot: full AI video for every shot is expensive (~$1.50 per 5-second clip on Seedance). Most of the savings come from changing what we make, not the tool.

AssetHowCost
Stills, character cards, carouselsGrok Imagine images (x.ai), reference-locked to character sheets$0.02–0.07 per image; <$0.50 per carousel
Episode shots (most)Stills with slow pan/zoom, layered motion, edited in-house~$0
Episode hero shots (2–3 per episode)Grok Imagine Video 1.5 (~$0.70/clip); Seedance only when a shot must be flawless (~$1.50)~$2–5 per episode
VoiceElevenLabs (paid plan required for commercial use), one voice per house; hired voice actor optional for the flagship~$5–22/month
MusicLicensed library or ElevenLabs music (paid)$0–20/month
GuardrailsEvery paid run quotes cost first and stops at a hard cap; every frame QA'd for consistency, text glitches, photorealism—

Estimated monthly total: ~$50–100 at 2 episodes/week plus statics. Human time: ~2 hrs/week review + ~20 min/day community.

Honest expectation: organic from zero is slow. We judge after 90 days of consistent posting. Monthly: double down on the character series with the best sends and follows; cut the weakest.

Decisions for the team

  1. Approve 'The Houses' and the Lake → Mountain → Beach rollout.
  2. Approve or rename the houses, families and character series.
  3. Owners: who approves posts (~2 hrs/week) and who answers comments and DMs (~20 min/day).
  4. Voices: ElevenLabs voices (cheap) or a hired voice actor for the Lake Cabin.
  5. Handle: keep @splithaus (recommended, so the following builds on the brand) or a separate series handle.
  6. Budget cap: suggested $100/month for generation and tools during the first 90 days.
Open risks: organic growth may be slower than hoped (mitigated by the 90-day review and trial reels); AI video costs and quality change monthly (mitigated by the cheap still-first pipeline); a competitor (SharedStead) already publishes family-cabin guides, so our edge must be character and community, not more guides.
